prompt:
Style: small-illustration. Transform the supplied ORIGINAL photograph of a LEGO Millennium Falcon model on a white cabinet, minifigures, a display plaque and nearby autumn foliage. Render only a single full-frame artwork using this style treatment:

The artwork extracts only the most recognizable subjects, contours, poses and narrative relationships and reinterprets them as a small-scale editorial spot illustration, aggressively eliminating secondary detail and background. Its defining principle: an exceptionally small illustration surrounded by an enormous amount of untouched paper — the drawing occupies only a small portion of its half, placed by the subject's natural direction and weight, with no background, panel, border or frame, and the paper itself as an active compositional element; when in doubt, remove more. People, buildings, animals, plants, objects and landscapes may be boldly generalized, cropped, omitted or recombined, but the correspondence with the photo above must read at a glance. The drawing uses restrained gestural strokes in rough, dry media — wax crayon, oil pastel, coarse graphite, China marker — a few powerful strokes, simplified shapes, broken contours, scuffs, incomplete coverage, exposed paper and slight misalignment: tactile, handmade, slightly imperfect. Color is strictly three elements: warm gray-white paper, charcoal black carrying the structure, contours and main visual weight, and rust red / brick red used only as a sparse selective accent at a few visual jump-points — distributed by the picture's rhythm, not matched to objects' real colors. Excluded: complete scene reconstruction, filled backgrounds, photorealistic redrawing, polished vector looks, multicolored rendering, complex shadows, cartoon or 3D feel, oversized headlines, templated poster feel. 

Preserve the original scene's subject relationships. Every part of the canvas must belong to the transformed artwork. No original photo panel, no before/after comparison, no split, no text.
